coverage.notes: SEL: no Massachusetts-adopted SEL standards found. DESE's SEL page says the Department commonly uses CASEL's definition and reproduces CASEL's five competencies with examples, so the framework recorded is CASEL's, as presented by DESE (guidance, not a state standard). POG: 'Vision of a Massachusetts Graduate' (6 attributes, 3 qualities) released Sept 24, 2025 by the Governor's Statewide K-12 Graduation Council; mass.gov calls it an aspirational outline and 'the first step' toward a new statewide graduation standard. I found no Board of Elementary and Secondary Education vote adopting it, and the graduation standard itself was still being worked out (search results mention June 2026 final recommendations that I did not open), hence 'in progress'. mass.gov returned 403 to our tools, so its text was read from an Internet Archive copy. Reviewer: check current status.

frameworks.name: CASEL Five Core Competencies of SEL (as presented on the Massachusetts DESE SEL web page)
frameworks.issuingBody: CASEL, as published by the Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education
frameworks.notes: Read DESE's SEL page (section 'Five Core Competencies of SEL, with examples noted'; page footer says last updated April 8, 2026). The page labels the descriptions as CASEL's and also says 'a range of other definitions ... are also viable'. This is NOT a Massachusetts standard and no adoption year is given. Items are paraphrases of CASEL's competency descriptions. Reviewer: decide whether to show this on the public page at all.

items.title: Self-Awareness
items.summary: Understand one's own emotions, thoughts and values and how they influence behavior; recognize strengths and limitations with a grounded sense of confidence and purpose.

items.title: Self-Management
items.summary: Manage emotions, thoughts and behaviors effectively in different situations and work toward goals, including delaying gratification, managing stress and feeling motivated.

items.title: Social Awareness
items.summary: Understand the perspectives of others and empathize with them, including people from diverse backgrounds, and understand social norms and the supports around one.

items.title: Relationship Skills
items.summary: Build and keep healthy, supportive relationships: communicate clearly, listen actively, cooperate, resolve conflict constructively, resist negative pressure and seek or offer help.

items.title: Responsible Decision-Making
items.summary: Make caring, constructive choices about behavior and social interactions, weighing ethical standards, safety and the consequences of actions for oneself and others.

frameworks.name: Vision of a Massachusetts Graduate
frameworks.issuingBody: Executive Office of Education / Statewide K-12 Graduation Council (Massachusetts)
frameworks.notes: Text read from an Internet Archive snapshot of the mass.gov page (web.archive.org/web/20260930070605/https://www.mass.gov/info-details/vision-of-a-massachusetts-graduate) because mass.gov blocked our fetch tools; the six attribute names and definitions match a Public Consulting Group draft dated Aug 19, 2025 hosted by massculturalcouncil.org. Released Sept 24, 2025 (per WBUR); no adoption year recorded because no Board vote was found. Qualities: Thinkers (AP, CPS), Contributors (SAN, IC), Leaders (EC, RDM). Codes are FNE-assigned.

items.title: Academically Prepared
items.summary: A strong foundation across academic disciplines, with the knowledge to thrive in college, career and civic life and the skills to keep learning.

items.title: Critical Problem-Solvers
items.summary: Examine information critically to draw connections, question assumptions, infer meaning and shape solutions.

items.title: Self-Aware Navigators
items.summary: Understand oneself, one's strengths and one's opportunities, and use unique skills to navigate a variety of paths and environments.

items.title: Intentional Collaborators
items.summary: Engage respectfully and productively with diverse individuals and groups, valuing one's own perspectives and identities and those of others.

items.title: Effective Communicators
items.summary: Express ideas confidently and clearly to diverse audiences across a variety of mediums.

items.title: Responsible Decision-Makers
items.summary: Set and pursue personal goals, make healthy and financially sustainable choices, and show confidence and competence in shaping one's life.

alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Feelings Detective" (sel domain, skill: Self-Awareness). FNE's catalog description: "Look at the clues in a scene, then pick every feeling that fits." Practises naming feelings from clues in a scene. Limit: Reads other people's feelings; no work on one's own thoughts and values.

alignments.framework: CASEL Five Core Competencies of SEL (as presented on the Massachusetts DESE SEL web page)
alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Strength Spotter" (sel domain, skill: Self-awareness). FNE's catalog description: "Notice what someone does, spot the strengths it shows, then think about your own." Players spot the strengths a person's actions show, then think about their own, which relates to recognising strengths. Limit: Strengths only; limitations and a sense of purpose are not covered.

Players name the values behind what someone does, then think about their own, which relates to understanding one's values. Limit: Values and identity; emotions and strengths are not the focus.

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (series: Conflict & Self-Government; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that emotions are beginning to take control, practice a simple pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful action that keeps their response aligned with their values." Students practise a pause-and-reset process and choose a respectful action, which is managing emotions and behavior in a hard moment. Limit: Emotion management; stress management, goal setting and delaying gratification are not part of the objective.

Students identify an immediate and a later consequence, who else is affected, and choose a caring action, which is anticipating the consequences of one's actions. Tune Your Brain game "Reading Detective" (literacy domain, skill: Reading Comprehension). FNE's catalog description: "Read the clues in a short mystery, pick your answer, then prove it with the text." Players read clues in a short mystery and prove their answer from the text, which practises reading comprehension. Limit: Practice of one literacy skill; it does not build a foundation across academic disciplines.

Tune Your Brain game "Quick Math" (math domain, skill: Numerical Reasoning). FNE's catalog description: "Solve arithmetic problems against the clock before time runs out." Players solve arithmetic problems against the clock, which practises numerical reasoning. Limit: Arithmetic fluency only; FNE is not an academic curriculum.

Tune Your Brain game "Critical Read" (literacy domain, skill: Critical Comprehension). FNE's catalog description: "Judge real claims for evidence, bias and sources, then prove your judgment from the text." Players judge claims for evidence, bias and sources and prove their judgment from the text, which is critically examining information and questioning assumptions. Limit: Reading-based; shaping solutions is not part of the description.

Players pick the most accurate headline and prove it with evidence from the text, which practises inferring meaning from information. Limit: A media-literacy exercise on short stories.
